macro.summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score -1 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl +; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +13.0%; weakest: Corn -16.0%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.12% (+11 bp in a month), 2-year 4.79% (+3 bp); 2s10s curve +33 bp (+8 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.07% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.68 (+1.2% in a month, +3.5% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.019 (-2.4% in a month): a firmer real slows Brazilian farmer selling and supports world prices. USD/CNY 6.664 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.59 (+7.9%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 +0.8% in a month (+12.7% YTD); VIX 17.1. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 97.50 $/bbl (+9.4% in a month), Brent 108.38, ULSD 4.652 $/gal (+3.7%), natural gas 2.85 (-4.6%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -3.2% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.0%, Hang Seng -5.6%, yuan +0.5% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 14 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (42%); S&P GSCI +1.2% in a month; gold -5.4%.
